data.title: Sextortion-Investment Hybrid Fraud — Small Payment Escalation to Crypto Addresses with Communication Pattern Shift
data.description: Detects the sextortion-investment hybrid fraud pattern where a victim makes initial small payments followed by escalating amounts to cryptocurrency addresses, with the communication pattern showing a transition from social/romantic interaction to financial urgency. INTERPOL's 2026 Global Financial Fraud Threat Assessment documents this as a globally escalating pattern where scam centre operators systematically pivot from romance/investment scripts to sextortion as a scripted operational fallback. The hallmark behavioral signature is a first-ever crypto transaction within 30 days of a new social media contact, followed by rapid escalation in both payment frequency and amount, often accompanied by messaging patterns shifting from casual/romantic to urgent/threatening language. The hybrid structure maximizes total extraction while suppressing victim reporting through shame and blackmail leverage.

detection.condition: selection AND filter_escalation_pattern AND filter_first_crypto AND filter_communication_shift

enrichment_required.source: Account transaction history analysis — true if customer had no crypto transactions prior to 60 days ago
Days since customer's first-ever cryptocurrency transaction
Days since last new social media or dating app contact event (requires platform data enrichment or customer-reported timeline)
Ratio of most recent transaction amount to first transaction amount in the 30-day window
Count of crypto transactions to same or related addresses in trailing 30 days

queries.cql:
// CrowdStrike CQL for Sextortion-Investment Hybrid Escalation
// Detects small-to-large crypto payment escalation following new social contact
(payment_type="cryptocurrency" OR payment_type="crypto_deposit" OR payment_type="wire_to_crypto_exchange")
is_first_crypto_period="true"
days_since_account_first_crypto<=60
| transaction_count_30d := count(transaction_id, span=30d)
| first_amount := min(amount, span=30d)
| last_amount := max(amount, span=30d)
| escalation_ratio := last_amount / first_amount
| where transaction_count_30d >= 3 AND escalation_ratio >= 3.0
| total_amount_30d := sum(amount, span=30d)
| unique_crypto_addresses := count(distinct=crypto_address, span=30d)
| groupBy(account_id, function=[
    collect([total_amount_30d, transaction_count_30d, escalation_ratio,
             first_amount, last_amount, unique_crypto_addresses,
             days_since_account_first_crypto])
  ])
| sort(total_amount_30d, order=desc)
queries.splunk:
`comment("Splunk SPL for Sextortion-Investment Hybrid Escalation")`
`comment("Detects escalating crypto payments following new social contact")`
index=flame_banking sourcetype=flame:transaction_monitoring
  (payment_type="cryptocurrency" OR payment_type="crypto_deposit" OR payment_type="wire_to_crypto_exchange")
  is_first_crypto_period="true"
  days_since_account_first_crypto<=60
| stats count AS transaction_count,
        min(amount) AS first_amount,
        max(amount) AS last_amount,
        sum(amount) AS total_amount,
        dc(crypto_address) AS unique_crypto_addresses,
        earliest(transaction_date) AS first_txn_date,
        latest(transaction_date) AS last_txn_date
  BY account_id
| where transaction_count >= 3
| eval escalation_ratio = last_amount / first_amount
| where escalation_ratio >= 3.0
| eval risk_score = case(
    escalation_ratio > 10 AND total_amount > 50000, "critical",
    escalation_ratio > 5 AND total_amount > 10000, "high",
    1=1, "medium")
| table account_id, transaction_count, first_amount, last_amount,
        escalation_ratio, total_amount, unique_crypto_addresses,
        first_txn_date, last_txn_date, risk_score
| sort - total_amount
queries.sql:
-- SQL for Sextortion-Investment Hybrid Escalation
-- Detects escalating crypto payments pattern characteristic of hybrid sextortion-investment fraud
WITH crypto_txns AS (
  SELECT
    t.account_id,
    t.transaction_id,
    t.amount,
    t.crypto_address,
    t.transaction_date,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t.account_id ORDER BY t.transaction_date ASC) AS txn_seq,
    COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY t.account_id) AS txn_count,
    MIN(t.amount) OVER (PARTITION BY t.account_id) AS first_amount,
    MAX(t.amount) OVER (PARTITION BY t.account_id) AS last_amount,
    SUM(t.amount) OVER (PARTITION BY t.account_id) AS total_amount,
    COUNT(DISTINCT t.crypto_address) OVER (PARTITION BY t.account_id) AS unique_addresses
  FROM transactions t
  JOIN account_crypto_history h ON t.account_id = h.account_id
  WHERE t.payment_type IN ('cryptocurrency', 'crypto_deposit', 'wire_to_crypto_exchange')
    AND t.transaction_date > CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '30 days'
    AND h.is_first_crypto_period = TRUE
    AND h.days_since_first_crypto <= 60
)
SELECT
  account_id,
  txn_count AS transaction_count,
  first_amount,
  last_amount,
  (last_amount / NULLIF(first_amount, 0)) AS escalation_ratio,
  total_amount,
  unique_addresses AS unique_crypto_addresses
FROM crypto_txns
WHERE txn_seq = 1
  AND txn_count >= 3
  AND (last_amount / NULLIF(first_amount, 0)) >= 3.0
ORDER BY total_amount DESC

references: INTERPOL Global Financial Fraud Threat Assessment, 2nd Edition, March 2026
INTERPOL GFFTA 2026 — Increasingly Hybrid Fraud Tactics and the Rise in Sextortion

falsepositives: Legitimate new cryptocurrency investor making progressively larger purchases as they gain confidence
Customer gradually converting savings to crypto for planned overseas relocation or property purchase
Recurring crypto purchases via dollar-cost-averaging strategy that happen to coincide with new social media activity
